completed_results.judge_comment: Scenario 1’s decisive Standard-G impossibility argument is factually wrong. It says B and C ‘cannot finish early enough for the only 2-hour October 19 GPU window, 15:00–17:00.’ GPU also has a 2-hour window at 10:00–12:00, and B/C can finish by 15:00 for the afternoon window (as the schedule itself does: C ends 15:00 and D runs 15:00–17:00). The conclusion is not validly supported.

validation_02_comments.comment: Both scenario justifications are factually consistent with the project data, approved changes, and the submitted schedule. Accelerated G at 14:00–15:00 yields a conflict-free A–N schedule finishing at the 10:00 deadline for cost 5. The cost-0 rejection is supported: the earliest A–B/C–D–F chain places F at 13:00–14:00, so 2-hour Standard G cannot finish before 16:00, leaving only 1 hour for the remaining 1.5-hour I–J/K–L chain, while M and N must occupy 09:00–10:00 on October 20. Budget 4 therefore excludes the only feasible method, and 10:00 is the earliest possible completion because M cannot start before October 20 at 09:00.

Both scenario justifications are factually correct, match the submitted schedule, and support the requested conclusions. The schedule is valid: Accelerated G is 14:00–15:00, all durations and prerequisites hold, and people and the single GPU and Review Room never overlap. M must start at 09:00 on October 20, so M 09:00–09:30 and N 09:30–10:00 is the only deadline-feasible placement and 10:00 is the earliest possible finish. The mandatory chain A–B–D–F–G–I–J–L is 7.5 hours with Standard G but October 19 has only 7 working hours, so cost 0 is impossible; Accelerated reduces it to 6.5 hours at cost 5. Scenario 2 is therefore infeasible because Accelerated costs 5 against a budget of 4, and the unapproved lunch, deadline, and skip-N changes do not apply.
